items.rationale: The internal frost fracture is covered under §2.4.3. Allow €65 gross for one like-for-like filling valve under §§7.1.9–7.1.10.
Section 7.1.9 covers connection elements that must be renewed with the fractured valve, even if they did not themselves fracture. Allow €22 gross for one standard hose.
Necessary labour to renew the internal fitting is covered under §7.1.9. Three hours at €88 gross per hour gives €264, consistent with the combined plumbing and leak-location allowance in Case 7.
Sections 7.1.7(e) and 7.1.9 cover consumables actually used on the valve repair, not general tool or overhead charges. Allow €14 gross for the repair consumables.
Sections 7.1.9 and 7.1.11 permit one attendance for the undertaking that carried out the covered repair. Allow €28 gross for that attendance, without a separate trip charge for leak detection.
Sections 2.4.5 and 5.2.2 expressly cover imaging used to locate the insured fracture. Allow €61 gross for equipment use alone, below the €2,500 gross per-event leak-location cap.

items.description: Exterior facade water and frost damage
items.rationale: Sections 3.1.4 and 3.5(a) exclude frost and weather damage to exterior finishes. The description separates this damage from the internal fitting fracture, so nothing is payable; the estimate is hypothetical for a small facade repair.
Sections 3.5(b) and 5.2.1 exclude removal of material from a surface whose damage is not covered. Nothing is payable; €35 gross is a hypothetical small removal charge.
Section 3.5(b) excludes renewal of the substrate beneath weather-damaged exterior plaster. Nothing is payable; €45 gross is a hypothetical allowance for a small patch.

Section 3.5(b) excludes other work on the same elevation, and §9.6 requires each charge to be tied to an insured affected part. No such connection is shown; €30 gross is a hypothetical minor-work allowance.
Section 3.5(b) expressly excludes preparing and re-forming the substrate beneath weather-damaged plaster. Nothing is payable; €50 gross assumes a small area if covered.

Sections 3.5(b)–(d) exclude recoating this facade regardless of the number of coats. The hypothetical €60 gross allows an ordinary like-for-like finish under §7.1.10, not four coats without evidence they were needed.
Sections 3.5(b) and 7.1.7(c) exclude drying the weather-damaged facade substrate because it is not an insured affected part. Nothing is payable; €45 gross is a hypothetical local drying charge.
Section 3.5(b) expressly excludes priming as part of renewing a weather-damaged facade finish. Nothing is payable; €25 gross is a hypothetical small-area priming charge.
Sections 3.5(c) and 7.1.11 exclude labour attributable to the uninsured facade work. Nothing is payable; the hypothetical labour total is five hours at €70 gross per hour.

Section 3.5(c) excludes flat-rate charges attributable to the uninsured facade work, and §7.1.8(b) also excludes standalone administrative overhead. Nothing is payable; €20 gross is a hypothetical minor ancillary charge.
